picks.why: A house begun in 1986 at Pyrgela outside Argos and settled since 2004 in a winery at Malandreni, one of the two Argolid communes of the Nemea zone; the Grande Cuvée, Agiorgitiko alone from high vineyards and first bottled in 1996 by the house's account, is its Nemea.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed in the thin run on the house's own pages (skouras.gr, read through search): founded in 1986 at Pyrgela, a village outside Argos, with rented vineyards; then a small winery at Gymno; then the winery at Malandreni in 2004, both villages inside the appellation, which Wines of Greece bears out (seventeen communes, fifteen in Corinthia with Gymno and Malandreni in Argolida). The house's sheet gives the wine as PDO Nemea, Agiorgitiko alone, first bottled in 1996, from vineyards at 1,040 metres; an American importer's listing adds red clay and twelve months in French barriques, half of them new. The vine age differs by merchant and the village of the vineyard was not found: confirm both from the technical sheet of the year taught. The label's word order varies on the house's own pages (Grande Cuvée Nemea on one, Nemea Grande Cuvée on another), so the pick holds Grande Cuvée alone, where the lane held Grande Cuvée Nemea: give the label in full. Megas Oenos, the first wine the house made, a blend of Agiorgitiko and Cabernet Sauvignon outside the appellation, goes in others with Saint George, its other Nemea. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Family estate at Ancient Nemea, by its merchants' accounts at work with Agiorgitiko since 1876 and among the district's first to farm organically; Palaia Klimata, Old Vines on the export label, is Agiorgitiko alone from an old section of its vineyard, held long in oak and bottle.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed in the thin run on the house's own label pages (papaioannouwines.gr, read through search): Palaia Klimata, Old Vines in English and Vieilles Vignes in French, Nemea PDO, Agiorgitiko alone, made at the family winery at Ancient Nemea from a chosen section of vines about forty years old, with eighteen months in oak and a year in bottle; a British merchant gives at least twelve months in French oak and twelve in bottle, so tell the regime by vintage. The house's German page spells it Palea Klimata. The year 1876 and the early organic farming come from merchants and Greek guides, not from a house page seen: hedge 1876 as a claim or leave founded empty, and confirm the certification before saying certified. The lane's line that the estate was among the first of the district to bottle its own wine was not tested in the thin run: say it only with two sources. Microclima, as the house spells its Nemea from a single plot, goes in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: The Nemea estate of the Mantinia house Tselepos: a vineyard of old Agiorgitiko at Koutsi bought in 2003 and named Ktima Driopi, with a small winery of its own; the Reserve, Agiorgitiko alone with a year in French oak, is its Nemea for the cellar.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed in the thin run on the family's own pages (tselepos.gr, read through search): 2003 is the purchase of the estate at Koutsi and the founding of Ktima Driopi; the vines were about fifty years old by the house (thirty five by one merchant), a part was replanted with clean Agiorgitiko and a small winery was built on the estate. The house lists the wine as Ktima Driopi Reserve, Nemea PDO, Agiorgitiko alone, twelve months in French oak, seven tenths of it new, and six months in bottle, from a vineyard it places at Dourmiza in Koutsi. The spelling is Driopi on the house's pages and Dryopi at a Greek merchant. The house gives the estate 380 metres and an American merchant about 1,250 feet: use the house's figure. The same family as the Mantinia pick Tselepos: a separate estate with its own name and wine, which the record says plainly. Driopi Classic, Cava Driopi and the rosé go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Small family winery at Petri, begun in 1997 by two accounts and in 1996 by a third, its vines farmed without irrigation or fertiliser; Monopati, the first of its premium wines, is Agiorgitiko alone under the appellation, aged in French oak.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not in the region record's producers line. Confirmed in the thin run: Monopati is sold as PDO Nemea, Agiorgitiko alone, by a Greek merchant and written up as Nemea by a Greek Master of Wine and on a British critic's site (the 2021: vines at 550 metres, twenty five days on the skins). The lane's 1996 is one merchant's year; a Greek food guide and the Greek Master of Wine give 1997: leave founded empty unless the house settles it. The vineyard: one plot at Daouliza in Koutsi since the 2014 vintage and Sikitsa before it, by the Master of Wine's notes; vines more than fifty years old by one merchant and nearing fifty by another: confirm both. The oak is fourteen or sixteen months in French barrels by vintage, and the wine is unfiltered by one listing. Whether the vineyard is certified organic is contested between listings: say dry farmed and no more. The wine named 4, from a vineyard said to predate phylloxera, Le Sang de la Pierre, Armakas and the estate Nemea go in others; confirm that Monopati and not 4 is the wine a guest meets. A father founded the house and his son, trained in Burgundy, makes the wine: name neither.

picks.why: Family winery founded in 1995 at Ancient Nemea, a short walk from the sanctuary, with a range that runs from a plain Nemea to regional blends; Ammos Terra Leone is its oak aged Nemea, Agiorgitiko alone from the family's own vineyard at Kokkinies.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS; the region record's producers line names the house, a lead and no proof. Added in the thin run as the fifth pick, because Gaia Wines is Santorini's pick and Semeli is Mantinia's. Confirmed on the house's own pages (palivos.gr, read through search): a family winery founded in 1995 at Ancient Nemea, when a modern winery took the place of the old treading tank, 800 metres from the archaeological site; Ammos Terra Leone is a dry red PDO Nemea of Agiorgitiko alone from the family's vineyard at Kokkinies and Stefani. A British merchant and a Greek wine magazine also date the house to 1995; one account says the vineyards had been the family's for a century and a half: hedge it. The label's words vary: Ammos Terra Leone on the house's pages and at a British merchant for the 2022, Terra Leone Ammos Reserve on a British critic's site for the 2020, Terra Leone Single Vineyard Selection Ammos Reserve in an Austrian magazine for the 2006, so the pick holds Terra Leone alone: give the label in full for the years taught, and say Reserve only where the label does. The ageing differs between the house's two pages (eighteen months in French oak and six in bottle; fourteen months in new French oak and amphorae and eight in bottle) and a merchant gives the 2014 eighteen months in new oak, four fifths French and a fifth American: tell it by vintage. Noema, the house's blend of Agiorgitiko, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah, is PGI Peloponnese and never its Nemea; it goes in others with Palivou Estate Nemea, the plain wine of the appellation. The house writes Palivou in English and Palivos in its address. Organic and biodynamic farming is a merchant's word: confirm before saying so. A founder and his two daughters appear on the house's pages: name none of them. Should a pick fall, the standby is the Nemea Wine Cooperative, founded in 1937 by retailers' accounts, whose Nemea Grande Reserve a British grocer sells as PDO: not confirmed on a page of its own.
